decisions.reason: As a bread product very close to the firm's core baking know-how, it fits its absorptive capacity well, so despite limited recent evidence it is more likely to be retained than withdrawn.
A sweet pastry draws directly on the firm's established confectionery skills and recipes, making it easy to refine and integrate into the range, so management would likely keep it.
This farmhouse bread is strongly related to the firm's traditional bakery base, and in a growing food market such a core-line extension would usually be kept unless clearly underperforming.
The poppy seed Christmas stollen is highly aligned with the firm's seasonal specialty competence and its gold award is a strong positive signal, so it is unlikely to be dropped.
The premium Christmas stollen builds on the firm's established seasonal expertise and was also gold-awarded, which supports continued marketing rather than withdrawal.
